Restated before interest: LLY paid $3,152mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2018 to 2025, 1.17% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 28.46% to 27.30%. Restated at replacement capex: LLY spent $23,144mm on plant over 2018 to 2025 against $7,255mm of plant depreciation, 5.89% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 27.30% to 20.25%. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Restated without working capital build: over 2018 to 2025 LLY's cash flow statement shows receivables up $15,658mm, inventories up $10,223mm, payables and accrued liabilities up $18,257mm, a working capital build of $7,624mm, 2.83% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 20.25% to 16.87%.

column11: JUDGEMENT. No Phase 3 is registered. NCT07533019 has primary completion 2027-05 (ClinicalTrials.gov, updated 2026-09-22). Lilly's own interval from a Phase 2 primary completion to its Phase 3 start is eloralintide's 6.5 months (NCT06230523 2025-05-30, NCT07282600 2025-12-15), so a Phase 3 starts about December 2027. Two vitiligo analogues: ruxolitinib cream went from its first Phase 3 start (TRuE-V1, NCT04052425, 2019-09-20) to vitiligo approval on 2022-07-18 (openFDA NDA215309 supplement 1, efficacy) and a first full year in 2023, 3.3 years; ritlecitinib's first vitiligo Phase 3 (NCT05583526) ran from 2022-12-01 to primary completion on 2026-02-05, 3.2 years before any filing or review. Their midpoint, about 4.2 years from a December 2027 start, puts the first full year in 2032

column11: ANCHOR, ruxolitinib cream (Opzelura), the last new mechanism to reach vitiligo, approved for it on 2022-07-18 (openFDA NDA215309 supplement 1). In Adiri 2026, 54 of the 366 patients with more than 10% of the body affected, 14.75%, had received a topical JAK inhibitor by the end of follow-up in November 2023, year index 1 of its vitiligo launch. Read as the share of the eligible pool on the drug in year index 1 and solved through the engine's identity on this pool (271,651; inflow 48,532 x 0.275 = 13,346), carryover 1.0, the Zeposia curve (k 1.005, midpoint 2.15) and this asset's 25.37% discontinuation: starts 14,409 and 33,264 over years 0 and 1, stock 14,409 and 44,018, which is 14.75% of 298,343 in year 1 at a peak of 0.489288. MULTIPLE 0.05, A JUDGEMENT: 0.05 x 0.489288 = 0.024464. For more: the first antibody against XCL1 and XCL2, aimed at the CD8 T cells behind the disease, where the JAKs act more broadly; Lilly sells two dermatology antibodies. Against: an infusion in clinic for a disease a cream and soon oral JAKs treat at home; ritlecitinib's vitiligo Phase 3 read out in 2026 and would be five years on sale by 2032; a 66-patient Phase 2 is the only test; and more than a quarter of US vitiligo patients take no treatment at all after diagnosis (Adiri 2026)
column12: the 0.05 multiple is the most arguable figure here.
